description: Fix Claude model category — all 5 entries are duplicate palmyra-x6 instead of actual Claude models
rationale: The Claude category has 5 identical palmyra-x6 entries — clearly a copy-paste bug. Users selecting 'Claude' from the dropdown get Palmyra instead, defeating the purpose of multi-LLM routing. This fix provides actual Claude model options.

description: Add retry logic for retryable network errors in llm_chat
rationale: The code already flags network errors as 'retryable' but never retries. With only 2 LLM calls in 7 days and 0 errors, adding a single retry for transient network issues improves resilience without risk of excessive retries.

description: Remove overly broad coding patterns that cause false model switches
rationale: Words like 'error', 'log', 'api', 'database', 'query', 'service', 'restart', 'deploy', 'test', 'async', 'await', 'thread' are extremely common in general conversation and would trigger coding model selection for almost any request. Removing these overly broad terms ensures the coding model is only selected for genuinely coding-related tasks, reducing unnecessary model switches and improving response relevance.

description: Reduce LLM_TIMEOUT from 180s to 120s to fail faster on hung requests
rationale: With avg LLM latency of 26.74s, a 180s timeout is excessively generous. Hung requests waste resources and block the bot. Reducing to 120s still provides ample headroom (4.5x the avg latency) while failing faster on stuck calls.

description: Reduce AGENT_TIMEOUT from 480s to 360s to prevent long-running agent loops
rationale: A 480s (8 minute) agent timeout is very long. With MAX_ITERATIONS at 30 and avg LLM latency of ~27s, 30 iterations could take up to 810s. But in practice, most agent tasks complete well under 360s. Reducing to 360s (6 minutes) prevents resource waste from runaway agent loops while still allowing complex multi-step tasks.

description: Fix MODEL_CATEGORIES 'Claude' entries — all are duplicates of palmyra-x6 instead of actual Claude models
rationale: The Claude category in MODEL_CATEGORIES contains five identical copies of 'writer/palmyra-x6' instead of actual Claude models. This means the !model dropdown shows fake Claude options that all route to Palmyra, misleading users and defeating the multi-LLM routing feature.

description: Add retry logic for retryable network errors in llm_chat
rationale: The code marks network errors as 'retryable' but never actually retries. With avg LLM latency of 25.89s, a transient network blip wastes a full round-trip. Adding a single retry with a 2s backoff improves resilience without significant cost.

description: Reduce LLM_TIMEOUT from 180s to 120s to fail faster on stalled requests
rationale: Average LLM latency is 25.89s. A 180s timeout means a stalled request blocks the bot for 3 minutes before failing. Reducing to 120s still provides ample headroom (nearly 5x the average) while failing faster on truly stuck requests, improving responsiveness.

description: Reuse pooled HTTP session in web_search instead of creating new session per call
rationale: web_search creates a new aiohttp.ClientSession per call. Reusing the pooled session eliminates TCP connection setup overhead for every web search, improving response time and reducing resource usage.

rationale: The streaming payload sets stream=True but relies on the non-streaming max_tokens being set earlier. Explicitly including max_tokens in the streaming payload ensures output is bounded even if the payload construction order changes, preventing runaway responses that consume tokens and latency.

description: Increase connection pool limit_per_host for LiteLLM proxy
rationale: All LLM and web search calls go through the same LiteLLM proxy host. limit_per_host=5 is too restrictive and can cause connection queueing under concurrent requests. Increasing to 15 allows parallel tool-call LLM requests without connection starvation.

description: Reduce session history window from 35 to 25 messages
rationale: With 35 messages in context, each LLM call sends a large payload contributing to the 22.83s average latency. Reducing to 25 messages cuts token usage by ~30% per call while retaining sufficient conversation context for a specialized bot with low daily volume.

description: Reduce LLM timeout from 75s to 60s
rationale: Average LLM latency is 22.83s with 0 errors. A 75s timeout is overly generous; 60s provides ample headroom (2.6x the average) while failing faster on truly hung requests, preventing the bot from appearing unresponsive.

description: Reduce MAX_ITERATIONS from 30 to 20 to prevent runaway agent loops
rationale: 30 LLM iterations at 22.83s avg latency could take up to 11.4 minutes per agent request. With AGENT_TIMEOUT at 480s (8 min), the iteration cap would never be reached anyway. Setting to 20 aligns with the timeout and prevents wasted API calls if the timeout is later increased.

description: Tighten coding detection patterns to reduce false positives
rationale: The words 'error' and 'log' are too broad — they match any mention of errors or logs in conversation, triggering unnecessary model switches to the coding model. Replacing 'log' with 'error log' and keeping 'traceback'/'exception'/'stack trace' narrows detection to actual coding contexts. This reduces unnecessary model routing overhead.

description: Reduce LLM timeout from 60s to 45s
rationale: Average LLM latency is 23.17s. A 60s timeout means stuck calls waste up to 60s before failing. Reducing to 45s still provides ~2x headroom over average latency while failing 15s faster on hung requests, improving overall responsiveness.

description: Reduce session history window from 25 to 15 messages
rationale: With 74 LLM calls over 7 days and avg latency of 23.17s, reducing the context window from 25 to 15 messages will decrease token usage and prompt processing time per call, directly lowering latency. For a low-volume admin bot, 15 messages of context is sufficient.

description: Reduce max iterations from 20 to 12
rationale: With only 8 tool calls in 7 days total, the bot rarely uses multi-step tool chains. Reducing max iterations from 20 to 12 prevents runaway agent loops while still allowing complex multi-tool workflows. This also caps worst-case latency at 12 * 23s ≈ 4.6min, well under the 480s agent timeout.

description: Reduce LLM retry delay from 2s to 1s
rationale: The 2s retry delay adds unnecessary latency when a transient network error occurs. With 0% LLM error rate, retries are rare, so reducing to 1s minimizes delay without meaningfully increasing retry storm risk.

description: Increase per-host connection limit for LLM proxy
rationale: All LLM calls go to the same LiteLLM proxy host, so limit_per_host=15 is the actual bottleneck. Raising it to 20 (matching the total limit) ensures concurrent requests across channels are never queued waiting for a connection slot.

description: Increase LLM timeout from 45s to 60s
rationale: Average LLM latency is 24.92s, meaning some calls likely approach the 45s timeout. Increasing to 60s reduces the risk of timeout failures on complex reasoning tasks, especially since llm_error_rate is currently 0.0 and we want to keep it that way.

description: Add keepalive_timeout and cleanup to TCPConnector
rationale: The bot restarts every ~1 hour and makes frequent LLM calls. Adding keepalive_timeout=60 ensures connections are reused efficiently across calls, and enable_cleanup_closed=True prevents leaked connections from half-closed sockets, improving resilience during the frequent service restarts visible in logs.

description: Increase retry delay from 1s to 2s for transient network errors
rationale: A 1s delay may be too short for transient network issues to resolve, especially when the LiteLLM proxy or upstream model providers are under load. Increasing to 2s gives the network stack more time to recover, improving the success rate of the single retry attempt.

rationale: With 190 LLM calls over 7 days and only 8 tool calls, most interactions are single-turn. Reducing max iterations from 12 to 10 prevents runaway agent loops from consuming excessive LLM calls and latency, while still providing ample turns for complex multi-step tasks. This caps worst-case latency at ~250s instead of ~300s.

description: Reduce session history window from 15 to 12 messages
rationale: With avg LLM latency of 24.92s, larger context windows increase token processing time per call. Reducing from 15 to 12 messages trims context size by ~20%, lowering per-call latency and token costs while still maintaining sufficient conversation context for a specialist bot that handles focused QA tasks.

description: Reduce LLM_TIMEOUT from 60s to 45s for faster failure detection
rationale: Average LLM latency is 23.31s. A 60s timeout means stuck calls can waste up to 37s beyond typical response time before failing. 45s provides ~2x headroom over average while failing 15s sooner on truly stuck requests.

description: Reduce AGENT_TIMEOUT from 480s to 360s to prevent excessively long agent loops
rationale: An 8-minute agent timeout is excessive for a dev/QA bot. With avg LLM latency of 23.31s and max 10 iterations, a single agent loop could take up to ~230s. 360s (6 min) still provides generous headroom while preventing runaway loops from consuming resources.

description: Reduce MAX_ITERATIONS from 10 to 7 to limit agent loop depth
rationale: With only 8 tool calls in 7 days, the bot rarely enters multi-step agent loops. 10 iterations is excessive and can lead to long-running loops consuming LLM budget. 7 iterations is sufficient for most dev/QA tasks while reducing risk of runaway loops.

description: Reduce TCPConnector limits and keepalive timeout to match actual traffic patterns
rationale: The bot makes only ~33 LLM calls/day on average, all to a single local LiteLLM proxy. 20 concurrent connections with 60s keepalive is excessive for this traffic pattern. Reducing to 10 connections and 30s keepalive conserves file descriptors and memory while still providing ample connection pooling.

description: Reduce LLM timeout from 45s to 35s to fail faster on hung requests
rationale: Average LLM latency is 20.84s. A 45s timeout is overly generous and means a hung request blocks the bot for 45s before failing. 35s still provides 1.7x headroom over average latency while failing ~10s sooner on stuck calls.

description: Reduce session history window from 12 to 8 messages to lower token usage and latency
rationale: With 20.84s average LLM latency, reducing context window from 12 to 8 messages cuts input tokens by ~33%, directly reducing LLM processing time and cost per call. 8 messages still provides sufficient conversational context for most interactions.

description: Reduce LLM max_tokens from 4096 to 2048 for faster responses
rationale: Most bot responses in a Discord context don't require 4096 output tokens. Reducing to 2048 cuts generation time roughly in half for the common case, improving perceived latency. Long responses that need more can still be split across multiple turns or use streaming.

rationale: Dr. Voss specializes in code quality and testing tasks. 2048 tokens often truncates code responses, requiring additional LLM round-trips that inflate latency. 4096 reduces truncation and follow-up calls.

description: Remove overly broad 'update' from coding detection patterns
rationale: The word 'update' appears frequently in non-coding contexts (e.g., 'update me on status', 'any updates?'). Removing it prevents false model switches to the coding model, avoiding unnecessary latency from model routing changes.

description: Remove overly broad 'service' from coding detection patterns
rationale: The word 'service' is too generic (e.g., 'service status', 'customer service'). 'systemd' already covers the service management use case more precisely, reducing false positives in model auto-routing.

description: Add model name to LLM API error log in llm_chat
rationale: When errors occur, knowing which model was being called is critical for debugging. Since the bot supports multi-LLM routing, including the model name in error logs improves observability and reduces time to diagnose issues.
